alignments.note: Waw to And.
Anarthrous participle used substantivally takes the supplied he that (rule 46), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Construct noun with the supplied the (rule 29).
Rectum with of (rule 19).
Cognate infinitive absolute takes the distinct intensifier surely (rule 56).

Finite verb with its resumptive subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), rendered by the light verb phrase put to death and headed on the complement (rule 44); discontinuous around the intensifier (rule 25).
Cognate infinitive absolute takes the intensifier certainly (rule 56).
Finite verb with its auxiliary, discontinuous around the intensifier (rules 17, 25).
The בְּ of רָגַם בְּ; the ASV writes a bare English object, leaving the preposition nothing (rule 40).
Object suffix to him (rule 18).
כֹּל to all.
Article to the.
Noun to congregation.

The first comparative preposition takes the whole opening expression as well; both Hebrew members write their own preposition, so each takes only the English written for it (rule 14). Head on the connective word under rule 24.
Assimilated article token takes the written the (rule 12).
Noun to sojourner.
The second comparative preposition takes the answering as.
Assimilated article token takes the written the (rule 12).
One substantive rendered by home born; rule 31's subtraction leaves home as the distinguishing word, born alone being generic. Heading on born was the competing reading.
Temporal בְּ before an infinitive construct takes the when (rule 52).
Infinitive construct to blasphemeth.
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun (rule 18).
Anarthrous noun with the supplied the (rule 15).

The italic of Jehovah repeats a genitive the second clause of the Hebrew does not write; no morpheme licenses it, so it is added under rule 30. The italics corroborate this without deciding it (rule 7).
Finite verb with its auxiliary, rendered by the light verb phrase put to death and headed on the complement (rules 17, 44).

review_notes: The as well ... as pair is not rule 14's correlative given to one connective: two comparative כְּ morphemes stand in the Hebrew, so each takes the English written for it.
The italic of Jehovah in the closing clause is added; the Hebrew there writes only שֵׁם.
